look_here_first: LOOK FOR NARROW, NEEDLE-LIKE LEAVES, THEN THE FRINGED CYATHIA. Beetle spurge is an erect/ascending 10–75 cm desert Euphorbia with ALTERNATE main-stem leaves, extremely narrow linear to linear-elliptic blades 20–55 × 1–3 mm, and 2–4 tiny teeth only near the leaf tip (can look entire). Its upper flowering bracts occur opposite/whorled, NOT evidence that whole plant is opposite-leaved. At the tip find a few hairy cyathia: usually 4–5 glands obscured by densely WHITISH-HAIRY appendages divided into many thin pointed fringes that FOLD INWARD OVER the glands. Capsule is relatively LARGE (4.4–4.9 mm), oblong to ovoid, gray-white hairy and sometimes mottled; genuine released seeds are 2.8–4.1 mm, black/gray mottled or pale, pitted and warty with a distinct caruncle. Compare E. exstipulata, whose white/pink appendages do NOT fold over the glands and whose leaves have clearly serrate margins.

taxonomic_note: Euphorbia eriantha Benth. is accepted in POWO. Distinct from creeping, opposite-leaved Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: this is an ascending desert Euphorbia in sect. Poinsettia, with alternate lower/midstem leaves, narrow green bracts and uniquely hairy, strongly incurved fringe-like gland appendages. State native TX; target county status remains unreviewed.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae, Euphorbia sect. Poinsettia (subsect. Erianthae). Cyathia are tiny cup-like reproductive units, not ordinary true-petaled flowers; fruit is a capsular spurge.
morphology_keys.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial with taproot; erect to ascending 10–75 cm; curving branches. Rocky desert washes and slopes, not a presumed common Hays County species.
morphology_keys.leaves: Main stem leaves ALTERNATE (basal node may appear opposite), 20–55 × 1–3 mm linear to narrow linear-elliptic with pronounced midvein; 2–4 tiny teeth close to the apex or practically entire to naked eye. Lower face sometimes short soft hairs; upper face often nearly glabrous.
morphology_keys.bracts: Upper flowering bracts 2–3, OPPOSITE or WHORLED, linear green and leaf-like, subtending terminal few-cyathium branches; distinguish these from the actual alternate main stem leaves.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Terminal cymose group, tiny hairs cover the involucre; 2–5 commonly 4–5 green-maroon shallowly cupped glands, 0.5–0.6 mm wide, commonly hidden by WHITE/gray dense hairy appendages folded inward over glands.
morphology_keys.gland_appendages: Extraordinary whitish hood-like appendages 0.5–1 mm, cut into 5–12 long fine subulate fingers, densely whitish-hairy, CURLING OVER glands, vs E. exstipulata appendages that do not cover glands.
morphology_keys.ovary_capsules: Oblong-ovoid approx 4.4–4.9 × 3.5–4.1 mm 3-lobed fruit, canescent (covered in short white/gray hairs) with sometimes hairless patches; much larger and hairier than a tiny sandmat's fruit.
morphology_keys.seeds: Mature true seeds oblong or ovoid, 2.8–4.1 × 2–2.4 mm, mottled black and gray or light brown, flattened dorsiventrally, coarsely tuberculate/pitted, with an obvious pale caruncle at attachment end. Do not confuse developing capsule patterns with detached seed surfaces.
best_field_traits: ALTERNATE, linear near-needlelike 2–5.5 cm × 1–3 mm leaves
Upper opposite/whorled GREEN leaf-like flowering bracts (not showy white bracts)
Tiny almost concealed terminal cyathia with HAIRY white appendages folded inward over glands
Large white-gray hairy, often mottled oblong 3-lobed capsules
Mature large 2.8–4.1mm visibly warted/mottled seeds with caruncle
Generally erect or ascending instead of creeping sandmat

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. exstipulata: narrower-to-ovate leaf blades usually CONSPICUOUSLY toothed, often opposite, cyathial appendages white/pink and divided but NOT bent to cover the glands; E. eriantha has exceptionally narrow nearly untoothed ALTERNATE foliage and densely whitish-hairy, inward-folded gland fringe. E. heterophylla has considerably broader variable leaves, glabrous capsules and different gland count/structure. E. cyathophora's showy upper bracts and gland structures differ; both bicolor and marginata have white-margined conspicuous upper bracts whereas eriantha has wholly green very narrow ones. E. eriantha is a regional arid West TX reference rather than assumed native in Hays.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Beetle spurge: alternate needle leaves → hairy hood-like cyathium → large hairy fruit
steps: Confirm ALTERNATE stem leaves below terminal flower groups. Leaf-like whorled/paired BRacts at tips are not evidence that the stem is opposite-leaved.
Check needlelike leaf 2–5.5 cm long, 1–3 mm wide, only 2–4 tiny terminal teeth visible under lens.
Photograph cyathium at 10–30×: separate actual gland from densely white-hairy fingered appendage folding over it. Do not label without a clear close-up.
Identify a developing roughly 4–5 mm HAIRY three-lobed capsule; do not mistake released seeds for fruit or vice versa.
Find ripe expelled seed with 1-mm scale: 2.8–4.1 mm dark/light mottled surface, prominent wartlike projections and a caruncle.
Contrast with E. exstipulata: distinctly serrate foliage and gland appendages not rolled over the gland.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Existing macro supports hairy fruit, narrow leaf, hairy reproductive cluster but cannot prove 5–12 microscopic finger segments on gland fringe or calibrated seed caruncle. Source local provenance and county nativity not independently certified; preserve any existing range holds.
